title: U.S. House · California's 19th Congressional District
area: The Central Coast, including Monterey, Santa Cruz, and San Benito counties and part of southern Santa Clara County.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 elections under Proposition 50, a mid-decade redistricting measure voters approved in a November 2025 special election.
In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Jimmy Panetta won 58.4% of the vote (127,294 votes) and Peter Verbica won 20.5% (44,590 votes), advancing them both to the November general election.

candidates.name: Jimmy Panetta
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2017; represented the 20th District 2017–2023, renumbered 19th District since 2023)

summary.text: Jimmy Panetta is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for California's 19th District, which runs from south San Jose through Santa Cruz and Monterey counties to northern San Luis Obispo County. A former prosecutor and Navy Reserve intelligence officer who served in Afghanistan, he was first elected in 2016 and sits on the Ways and Means and Budget committees.

background.text: Born in Washington, D.C., in 1969, and grew up on California's central coast, where he attended local public schools and Monterey Peninsula Community College. Wikipedia lists him as the son of former Secretary of Defense and congressman Leon Panetta.
Earned an A.A. from Monterey Peninsula College in 1989, a bachelor's degree in international relations from the University of California, Davis (1991), and a J.D. from Santa Clara University (1996).

Served in the U.S. Navy Reserve as an intelligence officer from 2003 to 2011. According to his official biography, he volunteered for active duty in 2007, deployed to Afghanistan in support of Operation Enduring Freedom, and was awarded the Bronze Star.

Worked as a State Department clerk and as a deputy district attorney in Alameda and Monterey counties. His official biography says that after returning from deployment he served on the board of the Veterans Transition Center, helped open Monterey County's first Veterans Treatment Court, and worked to establish the Central Coast Veterans Cemetery on the former Fort Ord.

First elected to the House in 2016 to succeed retiring Rep. Sam Farr, defeating Republican Casey Lucius; he represented the 20th District from 2017 to 2023 and has represented the 19th since redistricting. He is serving his fifth term.
Serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and the House Budget Committee, and is a Chief Deputy Whip in the 119th Congress and a member of the House Democratic Steering and Policy Committee.

According to his official biography, legislation he has passed into law includes measures on clean energy, forest and pollinator protection, support for frontline health care workers, hunger among military families, and legal services for homeless veterans, and he secured $1.4 billion in COVID-19 relief for the district. He is also the founder and co-chair of several caucuses, including the Agriculture Research Caucus, For Country Caucus and Naval Education Caucus.
His official biography says his wife, Carrie Panetta, is a Monterey County Superior Court judge and that they have two daughters educated in the same local public schools he attended.

priorities.text: Lists comprehensively addressing housing affordability as a top priority, including a Workforce Housing Tax Credit Act, a First-Time Homebuyer Tax Credit Act, and expanding low-income housing and rental assistance.
Lists border security funding combined with a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers and farmworkers as an immigration priority.
Lists continuing to protect Medicare, lower prescription drug costs, and expand the health care workforce as priorities.

positions.summary: Is a member of the Pro-Choice Caucus and signed a discharge petition to bring the Women's Health Protection Act to a vote.
positions.quote: As a proud member of the Pro-Choice Caucus, I'll continue to fight for the rights of women to make their own health care choices.

positions.summary: Helped author and pass the Inflation Reduction Act's clean-energy investments, which the office says are reducing carbon output.
positions.quote: I was proud to help craft and pass into law the Inflation Reduction Act, the most significant, ambitious investment in tools combating the climate crisis in history.

positions.summary: Supports more border officers, agents, technology and immigration judges while also supporting a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers and protecting DACA and TPS recipients from deportation.
positions.quote: Although I've always supported immigration reform for our Dreamers, Farmworkers, and their families, I've consistently stated that we also need more border security, as that isn't a binary choice.

positions.summary: Cosponsored the reintroduced Assault Weapons Ban, which would prohibit the sale, transfer, manufacture and importation of semiautomatic weapons and magazines holding more than ten rounds, and said reinstating it is an important step in addressing gun violence.
positions.quote: Reinstating the Assault Weapons Ban is an important step in addressing our country's gun violence epidemic

positions.summary: Cosponsored and co-led a War Powers Resolution to end U.S. military action in Iran, saying Congress must reclaim its constitutional responsibility over war.
positions.quote: No president should be able to take this country into prolonged conflict without the consent of the American people through their Representatives

positions.summary: Said Democrats are fighting to extend the enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies and to restore the Medicaid cuts in the One Big Beautiful Bill.
positions.quote: That's why Democrats are fighting to extend the ACA subsidies and restore the cuts to Medicaid.

positions.summary: Called for reclaiming Congress's authority over trade to stop the price increases from the President's tariffs, and for negotiations to stop tariffs.
positions.quote: We must start now with negotiations to immediately reopen our federal government, protect healthcare, stop tariffs, and reduce prices.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Trade Subcommittee) and the House Committee on Budget in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Peter Verbica
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2 top-two primary with 20.5% of the vote

summary.text: Peter Verbica is the Republican nominee for California's 19th District, a Santa Cruz County financial planner and author who advanced from the 2026 top-two primary. He previously reached the 2022 general election for the California Board of Equalization, District 2. He says his campaign focuses on affordability, water infrastructure and immigration reform.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Santa Clara University in 1983, a Master of Science from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1992, and a J.D. from Santa Clara University School of Law in 1999.
Works as a managing director, principal and Certified Financial Planner at Silicon Private Wealth, and has also worked as an adjunct professor of economics at San Jose State University.
Monterey County Now describes him as a Santa Cruz County resident and author of the book Hard Won Cowboy Wisdom.

Ran for California Board of Equalization, District 2, in 2022 as a Republican: he finished second in the June primary with 28.2 percent and lost the November general election to Democrat Sally Lieber, 69.8 percent to 30.2 percent.

Lists civic affiliations including chair of the investment committee of the San Jose Symphony Foundation and former roles with the Pine Ridge Association at Henry Coe State Park, the Los Gatos Masonic Hall Corporation, the Digital Bridges Committee and the Hakone Foundation.
Finished second in the June 2, 2026 primary with 20.5 percent, behind Panetta's 58.4 percent. He says he is a registered Republican who views himself as an independent thinker.

priorities.text: Names affordability as a top priority, calling for ending high state taxes, reforming CEQA to allow more housing, and lowering DMV fees.
Prioritizes water infrastructure, saying California voters approved billions for new reservoirs 'none of which were built,' needed to fight wildfires and support agriculture.
Calls for immigration reform that helps agriculture and high-tech businesses with a 'Bracero 2.0' program providing a clear, expedited path to legal employment.

positions.summary: Supports reforming California's CEQA environmental-review law to allow more housing to be built.
positions.quote: End California's high taxes, reform CEQA to allow for more housing

statements.quote: reform immigration in California which helps ag and high-tech businesses and provide a Bracero 2.0 program with a clear, expeditious path to legal employment.
statements.context: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

statements.quote: we need pragmatic energy and environmental policies—protecting places like Monterey Bay while ensuring safe, reliable, and affordable energy.
statements.context: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

statements.quote: Peter is a vigorous advocate for: • small government, • lower taxes, • transparency, • accountability, • immigration reform, • the sanctity of our Nation’s borders, • a strong national defense, • school choice, and • merit-based education.
statements.context: On his campaign website's About page (third-person campaign text)
